title: Corryhabbie Hills Circuit
listingBlurb: Moorland above Glenfiddich — some track, plenty heather. Option A for a full circuit; Option B if you want less faff.
summary: Suggested line only. Big open moorland day above Glenfiddich: tracks help a bit, heather and bog still do their thing. Two options in the data — A is the fuller round, B is shorter and easier to trim if the group’s flagging.

disclaimerSection.title: Suggested line only
disclaimerSection.body: Built from maps, anchors, and walking the ground — not a surveyed trace. Weather, legs, and the hill get the last word; if it’s telling you to do something simpler, listen.

weatherNote.title: Weather note
weatherNote.body: Dufftown side: cloudy most of the day, about 4°C first thing up to ~12°C later, maybe a shower early on.
weatherNote.supporting: Grey but fine for stomping about — don’t wait for golden hour.
weatherNote.disclaimerLabel: Rough planning note, not a mountain forecast.

whyThisRoute.title: Why this walk?
whyThisRoute.body: One moorland circuit with forks — not a tick list of every bump. West side gives the sweep; Corryhabbie’s the obvious high point; tracks on the way back keep the end from dragging.
callouts: A: fuller round when the group’s up for it.
B: shorter, easier to bail, more stop-and-chat energy.
whyThisRoute.supporting: Same hills, different appetite. Pick the line that matches legs and weather — no prize for suffering.

recommendationBlock.title: Rough take
lines: Decent visibility and folk are keen — A’s the shape that makes sense.
Late start, tired legs, or just out for air — B’s fine; own it.
recommendationBlock.supporting: Clag or soggy ground hits B less hard. Good day and good legs — A earns its tea.

qualityMeter.headline: Decent chance of a good yin
qualityMeter.verdict: Open hill, two usable lines, weather’s alright — bog, heather, and flat light can still make it a slog.

factors.label: Flexible route choice
factors.note: Two lines in the data — you can trim the daft bits if you need to.

factors.label: Weather is usable
factors.note: Grey beats howling rain for this sort of ground.

factors.label: Broad moorland ground
factors.note: Big and open — can feel empty in flat clag.

factors.label: Bog / heather tax

factors.label: Social-day potential
factors.note: Suits a lazy start and plenty of sit-downs.

subscores.note: Big sky country — still feels like a hill day even when the light’s flat.

subscores.note: Late starts, chat, a few puff stops — you’ll get something out of it.

parkingNote: Parker about NJ 26906 32380. Don’t block gates, farm access, or anything a tractor might need.
anchorRefsIntro: Rough bearings for nattering and map checks — not turn-by-turn.

routeOptions.name: Option A — Full round
routeOptions.reason: Full circuit — west done early, tidier finish later.
routeOptions.lineDescription: Start from the parker (NJ 26906 32380), get Hill of Achmore out the way first, then sweep across Càrn a’ Bhodaich, Cairn Dregnie, Carn an t-Suidhe, curve back through the broad ridge ground toward Muckle Lapprach, then finish the main business on Corryhabbie Hill before using the tidier return lines back out.
routeOptions.whyPick: Feels like a full day’s loop, not a nip round one top. Weather and legs playing ball — this is the one.
routeOptions.tradeoff: More heather, more bog roulette, more commitment. Less fun if half the group’s knackered before the car door shuts.

routeOptions.name: Option B — Looser / easier day
routeOptions.reason: Best bits without every bump — easy to shorten if folk are fading.
routeOptions.lineDescription: Start from the parker (NJ 26906 32380), take Hill of Achmore, head up for Muckle Lapprach, carry on to Corryhabbie Hill, and then either call that good enough or tack on an extra bit if everyone still fancies it.
routeOptions.whyPick: Hits the good stuff without hoovering every contour. Shorten it, chat through it, or bail if the day goes sideways.
routeOptions.tradeoff: Doesn’t feel as “done” as the full round. If you need a neat circuit for the soul, this is the lazier option — sometimes that’s the point.

goodStopsDetail.intro: Decent places to stop for a puff or a regroup.

spots.title: Corryhabbie Hill
spots.description: Highest-feeling perch. If you’re stopping to stare, do it here.

spots.title: Muckle Lapprach shoulder
spots.description: Sit down without feeling you’ve left the day behind.

spots.title: Track junction near NJ 28983 28035
spots.description: Handy regroup — work out if anyone’s still keen or just bluffing about the finish.

whatDayFeelsLike.title: What the day’s like
whatDayFeelsLike.body: Big open hill. Nothing technical. Room to choose your own nonsense. Enough track to stay sane, enough peat and heather to remind you where you are.
whatDayFeelsLike.supporting: Good day: cruise big ground, stop where it looks nice, don’t overthink. Bad day: “that looked drier from back there,” wet sock, quiet swearing.
summaryLines: could be boggy nonsense in places
still a decent social hill day

terrainDetail.title: Terrain & vibe
terrainDetail.body: Open hill, heather, and a fair chance of bog. Nothing technical — just how much shite you fancy adding.
terrainDetail.supporting: Good bits: open and easy. Bad bits: peat, tufty grass, false confidence. Tracks nearby keep it from going full mission mode — fine for a relaxed team day.

wildlifeIntro: What lives up here and what the ground’s hinting at.

wildlifeCards.title: Red grouse
wildlifeCards.body: Very on-brand for this sort of heather moorland. If you see one explode out the heather and nearly take your head off, that’s about right.
wildlifeCards.whyItMatters: Tells you you’re in proper moorland country.

wildlifeCards.title: Meadow pipit
wildlifeCards.body: Small, brown, streaky, and easy to miss until one flutters up and gives itself away.
wildlifeCards.whyItMatters: One of the most likely birds you’ll actually notice if you’re paying attention.

wildlifeCards.title: Red deer
wildlifeCards.body: Always a realistic shout in Scottish upland country if you actually look up once in a while.
wildlifeCards.whyItMatters: Makes the whole place feel bigger and a bit wilder when you spot one.

wildlifeCards.title: Heather / blaeberry / bog moss / cottongrass
wildlifeCards.body: This is the proper texture of the hill. Lovely to look at, and sometimes a decent clue that the next few metres deserve suspicion.
wildlifeCards.whyItMatters: Helps you read the ground and explains why some bits feel great and some bits feel like a trap.

lookoutGalleryIntro: Grouse if the heather’s awake, pipits fluttering about, deer if you look up. Underfoot: heather, blaeberry, peat, cottongrass in the wet bits — fine till your foot disappears.
